result.title: A Cardiorespiratory Foundation Model Pretrained on Ten Physiological Signals for Perioperative and Critical Care
result.summary: Arterial, venous, pulmonary artery and intracranial pressures and ventilator waveforms guide decisions in operating rooms and intensive care units, yet foundation models for physiological waveforms have been built almost entirely on the electrocardiogram and photoplethysmogram. We present CARMEN, a single encoder pretrained without labels on ten cardiorespiratory waveforms (2.27 million modality-hours). CARMEN accepts any combination of co-recorded signals from 10 s to 5 min, and a conditioning mechanism, LSCNorm, restores the absolute signal level that normalization removes; without it, the AUROC for intraoperative hypotension fell from 0.894 to 0.780. Across 19 tasks from Korean and US cohorts, the frozen encoder outperformed supervised models on 12 of 15 and three foundation models, one general-purpose and two for biosignals, on 14 to 17 of 19, with none exceeding it on any task. Given the electrocardiogram or photoplethysmogram alone, it matched or exceeded signal-specific foundation models in most comparisons, and it retained its performance when channels were missing.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CARMEN，一个在十种心肺生理波形上无标签预训练的单编码器，配合恢复归一化所去除绝对信号水平的 LSCNorm，用于围术期与重症监护的多任务预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 属临床生理信号基础模型，评估指标是低血压等监护预测的 AUROC，不涉及视觉细节保持、latent 推理状态生成、证据筛选或停止决策；LSCNorm 的「恢复归一化丢失信息」仅是信号表征技巧，与 LVR 的状态与贡献分配问题缺乏实质联系。
